_what_this_is: For each capability primitive, the specific setting, script or configuration that narrows it, what it costs you, and the tier the control reaches afterwards. Guidance is free and stays free: guidance that costs money is guidance nobody follows (brief v0.33.64, the strategy brief). Efforts are borrowed from the assess library's controls, where they were written with the friction stated.

read.file.host.setting: run the agent in a container with only the project mounted, or under a separate user account
read.file.host.costs: an afternoon, then ongoing friction (container) · days, and it fights you (account)

write.file.host.setting: the same container or account; the tool's own directory restriction is a setting anything running as you can step around

delete.file.host.setting: the same container or account; and a backup that the agent cannot reach, because delete at host reach is irreversible
delete.file.host.costs: as above, plus a backup outside the grant

execute.process.host.setting: keep the confirmation prompt on for commands, and run in a container: execution survives inside it and stops being execution on your machine
execute.process.host.costs: a click per command · an afternoon for the container

send.endpoint.world.setting: route outbound traffic through an allow-list — the one control the hosted container already has, demonstrated rather than claimed
send.endpoint.world.costs: an hour, if you already have somewhere to put it

send.endpoint.allowed.setting: shorten the list; a host it does not need is a host it can reach
send.endpoint.allowed.costs: minutes per host, and a failure the first time it needs one you removed

read.credential.host.setting: keep credentials out of the account the agent runs as: a credential helper, a separate account, or a container without your home mounted
read.credential.host.costs: an afternoon, and re-authenticating where the agent needs a credential of its own

authenticate-as.credential.tenant.setting: scoped, short-lived tokens issued to the agent rather than your own; read-only where read is all it needs
authenticate-as.credential.tenant.costs: an hour per service, and rotation

authenticate-as.credential.signing.setting: a signing key of the agent's own, so its commits are signed as it and not as you (the registry's identity records exist for this)
authenticate-as.credential.signing.costs: an hour, and a second key to manage

grant.credential.self.setting: settings owned by a different user than the one the agent runs as, or set above the session by the platform
grant.credential.self.costs: minutes, if the platform supports it; otherwise the separate account

write.repository.tenant.setting: a branch protection rule at the host — the agent cannot edit it — and a pre-push hook in the clone for the earlier, cheaper refusal
write.repository.tenant.costs: minutes; and a review step before anything deploys

write.repository.project.setting: none needed for most work; a review before merge is the control

create.record.world.setting: no publishing token in the agent's environment; publish from CI with a token the agent does not hold
create.record.world.costs: an afternoon to move the publish step

send.message.world.setting: no mail or chat connector, or a connector that drafts and never sends

read.message.tenant.setting: a connector scoped to one folder or label, or none

write.budget.tenant.setting: a spend cap at the supplier, set by somebody other than the agent — the supplier has a reason to refuse: it is paying
write.budget.tenant.costs: the work stops when the cap is reached, which is the point

create.schedule.host.setting: no scheduler in the agent's environment; anything that outlives the turn goes through a person

read.record.history.setting: history off, or a fresh environment per task, so the grant is a tree over the present rather than a union over every prior turn

execute.process.self.setting: already a sandbox; keep it one

read.file.project.setting: none: this is what it is for

read.record.browsing.setting: grant the extension access on click, or on a list of sites, instead of on all sites; remove the ones you do not use
read.record.browsing.costs: a click the first time on each site
